books.name: Rocket
books.description: A lottery, not a strategy: 1 000 dollars that try for 10 000 in three months by buying USO calls when the Dynamic is long and USO puts when it is short, half the account on each bet, opened only when Kalshi's odds of a de-escalation moved over the week the way that bet needs (down for a call, up for a put). The life ends at the target, ten times its start. A model of the rule since 2011 reached it in fewer than three windows of three months out of a hundred, almost all in oil crashes; the typical window ended at two thirds of the account and four in ten too small to bet. Out of every total, never promoted; a reset starts a new life at 1 000 dollars.

rule.label: de-escalation index
rule.text: The mean probability, on Kalshi, that within 90 days the strait is back to normal, the US and Iran meet at senior level and they sign a nuclear deal (read off each deadline ladder, markets quoted within 10 cents). Its change over 7 days, times -2 per point, is the sleeve: de-escalation rising means short oil, falling means long; under 1 point, no view. Capped at +-20. No backtest in the desk's replay: the books on it are judged on their live fills only and are never promoted.

indices.label: de-escalation index

rule.label: de-escalation index
rule.text: The mean probability, on Kalshi, that within 90 days the strait is back to normal, the US and Iran meet at senior level and they sign a nuclear deal (read off each deadline ladder, markets quoted within 10 cents). Its change over 7 days, times -2 per point, is the sleeve: de-escalation rising means short oil, falling means long; under 1 point, no view. Capped at +-20. No backtest in the desk's replay: the books on it are judged on their live fills only and are never promoted.

indices.label: Fed path
indices.note: Fed path +21 bp on 2026-10-23 against +28 bp on 2026-10-16 (2 of 2 components in both): -7.1 bp -> sleeve +17.9 (-2.5 per bp)

rule.label: Fed path
rule.text: The expected change of the Fed's target rate over the FOMC meetings within 90 days, on Kalshi: each meeting's outcome markets (cut or hike by 25 or more, hold; quoted within 10 cents) weighted by their odds, summed in basis points. Its change over 7 days over the meetings both readings have, times -2.5 per basis point, is the sleeve: expectations turning dovish is a positive value, hawkish negative; under 1 bp, no view. Capped at +-20. No backtest in the desk's replay: the books on it are judged on their live fills only and are never promoted.

indices.label: recession probability
indices.note: recession probability 19.5 % on 2026-10-23 against 20.4 % on 2026-10-16 (1 of 1 components in both): -0.8 points -> sleeve +0.0 (inside the deadband of 1.0 points)

rule.label: recession probability
rule.text: The probability, on Kalshi, that a US recession begins within 365 days, read off the yearly NBER markets as one ladder by year end (markets quoted within 10 cents). Its change over 7 days, times +4 per point, is the sleeve: the odds of a recession rising is a positive value; under 1 point, no view. Capped at +-20. No backtest in the desk's replay: the books on it are judged on their live fills only and are never promoted.

oracle.source: Kalshi (public trade API), the desk's own daily archive (state/desk/kalshi-*.jsonl)
oracle.disclaimer: The reading of a UTC day is the first of that day, about 00:20 UTC - the previous evening in New York: the books read last night's prices, as the macro sleeves read yesterday's close. A book's forecast is the mean of its sleeves with the sign shown; long-only fund books stay in cash on a negative one.

analyst.state_text: The runner has no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret, so no reading is taken; the books stay in cash.

rule.text: Once a day on a US business day, after 13:00 UTC: claude-sonnet-5-5 searches the news since the previous business day's morning, at least 48 hours back (at most 6 searches), and writes a brief of the facts with their sources; a second call reads the brief alone and gives oil, gold, the S&P 500 and long Treasuries a forecast from −20 to +20 for the next five sessions. A book reads the newest reading of its decision day or the 3 days before; older, it closes. No backtest can exist: a model trained on the past knows the prices a replay would ask it to forecast. Paper only; the prior is that it has no edge; never promoted.

analyst.disclaimer: A language model's reading of the news for a paper-trading study: not advice, not a verdict.

prediction_markets.unit: price of a contract paying 1 $ = the crowd's probability
prediction_markets.note: No book trades on these markets: there is no history to test a rule on. The tick reads them every hour and archives one reading a day (state/desk/kalshi-*.jsonl); the first test is possible in a year.
